verdict.rationale: Fellow's own REST API covers the core meeting objects. It can read and write note agendas (with round-tripping Fellow Markdown), list notes, recordings and action items, complete or archive action items, upload recordings, delete notes as super admin, and register webhooks. Nothing documents API parity with the UI, and many UI features show no API equivalent, so only part of the story is delivered. Missing for 10: an explicit UI-parity claim; API coverage of recording, retention and workspace policy settings, keyword tracking, transcript redaction and Ask Fellow; creating or deleting action items and notes for regular users (note deletion is super-admin only); independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Developer API opens that data to you: transcripts, structured notes, and more, all available through standard REST calls.
Write a note's agenda and/or rename the note.
The format round-trips: the `content_fellow_markdown` you read from a note is exactly what you can send back to `POST /note/{id}/agenda`.
Mark an action item as complete or incomplete.
Upload a recording from a URL. Use this endpoint to bring an existing meeting recording into Fellow.
Only users with super admin privileges can delete notes through the API.
